bds-record:admin-config.reason: variables.names lists the variables in the order of variables.json on JSPrismarine, where BDS lists them in the order of its hash map: ["zebra","text","number","flag","nothing","object","apple","list","integer"]. Every value variables and secrets return, each SecretString and every transferPlayer call match BDS.

bds-record:block-inventory.reason: A diamond sword with 7 damage, put into a chest and read back with getItem, throws "Failed to get property 'damage'." from its durability component on BDS, where JSPrismarine returns 7. Every other container read and write, the inventory component of a chest, a barrel and stone, and the durability component of a new stack match BDS.

bds-record:block-members.reason: getMapColor gives one color per type, from the dump world's biome and the default permutation, where BDS tints grass by its biome and colors a log by its axis (issue #3299). Every neighbor, tag, localization key, item, liquid answer, setWaterlogged and isWaterlogged, isSolid, getParts, trySetPermutation, component list, withState error and registry read matches BDS.

bds-record:block-world-components.reason: The sign, piston, jukebox and cauldron components (issue #3302), the redstone producer and note block instrument components (issue #3303), liquidCanFlowFromDirection (issue #3304) and a bundle's item container (issue #3305) throw NotImplementedError on JSPrismarine, which gives the script host no seam to those systems yet. canPlace matches BDS.

bds-record:dimension-blocks.reason: getSkyLightLevel under a one-block roof: JSPrismarine's light follows Java, where sky light reaches the block under a one-block roof from the open sky beside it, one level down, where BDS gives it the full 15. getLightLevel under glowstone: Glowstone is an opaque block in Java, so the block under it reads its 15 block light one level down, where BDS lets the sky through it.

bds-record:dimension-volumes.reason: getBlocks with closest picks among blocks at one distance as BDS does, walking the volume x, then z, then y into a max-heap of the size asked for, for every captured case but three: from (5.5, 31.5, 5.5) the nearest 10 and 19 of a 3x3x3 cube, and from (7, 31, 5) the nearest 2, each pick a different block of a tied ring (issue #3317).

bds-record:custom-command-errors.reason: A custom command's argument that does not parse, and a command name the tree does not hold, fail with Brigadier's message on JSPrismarine, such as "Expected integer at position 10" and "Unknown command at position 0", where BDS words them "Syntax error: Unexpected \"seven\": at \"jsp:count >>seven<<\"". Every command that parses runs as on BDS, as the custom-commands scenario records.

bds-record:custom-components.reason: /setblock of the block already standing there counts one success on JSPrismarine, where BDS counts none. Every registration, error and hook, with its event, parameters and tick, matches BDS.

bds-record:entity-events.reason: Entity.kill on an armor stand raises entityHurt and entityDie on JSPrismarine, where BDS breaks it and raises neither. Every entitySpawn, the other blows, their damage after the grace period, their causes and the event order match BDS.

bds-record:world-event-gaps.reason: JSPrismarine has no world clocks, script-registered dimensions, pack settings, sound lengths, tripwire or target block redstone, input permissions or entity upgrades, so the world events that report on them and startup's dimension and world clock registries throw NotImplementedError, where BDS lets a script subscribe to each and hands it both registries.

bds-record:jsp-detect.reason: import @jsprismarine/server: JSPrismarine resolves an undeclared @jsprismarine/server. server: a pack that gets @jsprismarine/server uses it, its performance, getPing, bossBars, playerList, config and permissions included, and @jsprismarine/placeholders beside it, and takes the fallback only where the import rejects. import ./static.js: modules under @jsprismarine/ need no manifest entry, so a static import of one resolves.

bds-record:module-resolution.reason: import @jsprismarine/server: JSPrismarine resolves an undeclared @jsprismarine/server, so a pack can detect it and fall back on BDS.

bds-record:script-event-console.reason: The console trims the end of a line it runs, so /scriptevent jsp:last  two  spaces  gives the message "two  spaces" where BDS keeps "two  spaces ". Every other id, message and source matches BDS.

bds-record:world-basics.reason: A command a script runs fails with Brigadier's message on JSPrismarine, such as "Unknown command at position 0: <--[HERE]", where BDS words it "Syntax error: Unexpected \"jspnosuchcommand\": at \">>jspnosuchcommand<<\"", and JSPrismarine's /time set takes "nonsense" where BDS refuses it. The players, dimensions, success counts and the scriptEventReceive event match BDS.

bds-record:world-pending.reason: A playing sound's pause, resume, volume, pitch, fade, seek and stop, StructureManager.getPackStructureIds and placeJigsawStructure throw NotImplementedError on JSPrismarine, which sets no sound handle and loads no pack structures or Bedrock jigsaws. Dimension.poiManager's runtime condition error and placeFeature of a pack's feature match BDS.

bds-record:world-settings.reason: game rule defaults: A world starts spawnRadius at 10 and tntExplosionDropDecay off, the values the pinned BDS writes to level.dat and sends clients in GameRulesChangedPacket, and a script reads the rule the world holds. BDS's Script API reads 0 and true for the two. server defaults: JSPrismarine's random ticks follow Java's random_tick_speed, whose 3 draws per section a world starts with, since Bedrock's 1 names only a relative speed, and a level shows coordinates. set every game rule: The script raises each number by 3 and flips each boolean from what it read, so the two rules start from the world defaults, 10 and off, where BDS starts from 0 and true. game rules after the commands: A gamerule command writes back the value the script set, so tntExplosionDropDecay keeps the flipped world default.
